reason: The declaration states the negation of the canonical universally quantified population-centred non-strict tail assertion. This is a genuine refutation of the printed assertion, not a refutation of an alternative reading: the explicit IntervalExample law has continuous W, binary outcomes, consistency, unconfoundedness, strict positivity, known true propensity, independent product sampling, n=100 and alpha=10^-7. Its strict closed-interval noncoverage is about 1.19792910698e-7, already exceeding alpha. See scratch/T6-witness.md and the independent exact multinomial enumeration. Refutation of this universal validity clause suffices; the theorem does not claim failure at every confidence level.

Includes integrability and unbiasedness at every n>=1, uniform root-n tightness over every class with a common positive delta, and the fixed-law normal limit with exactly E[m(W)/pi(W)]-mu^2 as summand variance. The common-delta quantifier is explicitly part of canonical definitions_needed. Zero-variance Gaussian limits are handled as point masses. The stored measurable, bounded conditional-mean version imposes no substantive extra model condition. The actual iid law, binary consistency and separate potential-outcome unconfoundedness match the standing assumptions. The additional finite_lemmas are audit history and impose no extra statement clauses.

States every unbiasedness and proof-chain assertion in the canonical statement, using the exact adjusted estimator and fits measurable in opposite-fold observed triples only. It additionally permits every deterministic partition, covering roughly equal partitions, and asserts unbiasedness under integrability of the entire estimator even when separate predictions need not be integrable. The separate expectation chains have precisely the necessary usual integrability guards; conditional independence is unguarded. This strengthens the claim without replacing or weakening any clause.

Both independent implications match definitions_needed: extended mean-square L2 prediction convergence to two possibly different fixed L2 functions gives fixed-law root-n tightness; extended L2 consistency in probability to the true regression gives the normal limit with the numerical Hahn variance. Fixed L2 limits implement the usual finite-second-moment interpretation of mean-square convergence, with no regression-correctness assumption in part (b). There is no finite-sample L2 guard on fitted functions, and infinite errors are not collapsed to zero. Canonical definitions_needed explicitly defines attainment as this normal limit; no additional semiparametric optimality machinery is a clause. Balanced deterministic folds and opposite-fold dependence match the setting. The finite_lemmas are not extra clauses.

Quantifies over exactly measurable sequences of observed-data estimators without a propensity argument. The quantifier order forall estimator, exists eps>0,c>0, forall N, exists n>=N positive and valid law with failure probability >=c is equivalent to the canonical positive limsup of supremal failure probabilities. The class contains all standing-assumption laws with some positive delta per law, precisely as definitions_needed specifies; a common-delta Uniform(0,1) lower-bound construction appears only in finite_lemmas and is not a required statement clause. The target is E[Y(1)], not an ATE or sample-conditional mean.
